      <title>Trump establishes committee to investigate Fed governor Lisa Cook</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/oct/09/trump-investigate-lisa-cook-fed-governor</link>
      <description><p>US president renews his efforts to oust Cook despite supreme court ruling that her firing was unconstitutional</p><p>Donald Trump announced on Friday that he is establishing a committee to investigate Lisa Cook, the US Federal Reserve governor, over allegations that she committed mortgage fraud, renewing his efforts to oust her despite <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/jun/29/supreme-court-trump-lisa-cook-ruling">a June supreme court ruling</a> that her earlier firing was unconstitutional.</p><p>Trump said a committee will consult with justice department officials to decide whether there is “cause” for her removal. The White House will hold an in-person hearing on 5 November to consider the allegations against Cook, which will be closed to the public but transcribed and published. Cook will be able to submit a written statement to present her own evidence and will be subject to examination from White House and her own legal counsel.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/oct/09/trump-investigate-lisa-cook-fed-governor">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Trump immigrant purge could cut social security for Americans by $2,000 a year</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/09/trump-immigration-cost-social-security</link>
      <description><p>New report on economic cost of anti-immigration campaign projects 8.6% reduction in retirement payments by 2034</p><p>Elderly Americans can expect to lose an average of $2,152 in annual social security benefits each, a projected 8.6% reduction in their retirement payments, by 2034 and every year after as a direct consequence of the economic fallout from the Trump administration’s <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/series/ice-2-0-inside-trumps-new-immigration-dragnet">anti-immigration campaign</a>, if that carries on, according to a new report shared exclusively with the Guardian.</p><p>Already, US food prices are up, housing permits to build new homes are down – and even native-born Americans are losing out on potential jobs after the sudden exodus of 1.2 million foreign-born workers over the last two years as a result of Donald Trump’s policies, the report finds.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/09/trump-immigration-cost-social-security">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Trump made ‘clear’ that media ban was due to critical coverage, court told</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/media/2026/oct/08/trump-media-ban-hearing</link>
      <description><p>Lawyer for CNN, MS Now and Politico says Trump admitted he banned networks from White House over their coverage</p><p>Donald Trump continues to be the strongest witness for the media companies arguing that they were unfairly barred from the White House at his direction, a lawyer representing CNN, MS Now and Politico told a federal judge on Thursday afternoon.</p><p>The media coalition was in court asking the judge to extend the temporary restraining order (TRO) he issued on 24 September requiring the White House to lift the ban for 14 days. That temporary reprieve was scheduled to expire on Thursday, but district court judge Timothy Kelly, a Trump appointee, said he would extend it until Tuesday and that he would probably rule on a motion for a preliminary injunction by that day. That means the White House will be forced to allow journalists from CNN, MS Now and Politico to continue accessing the building until at least Tuesday.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/media/2026/oct/08/trump-media-ban-hearing">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>The project has sparked doubts over whether the plant will be built and delivered as promised, given Trump’s record</p><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/donaldtrump">Donald Trump</a> has long sought to portray himself as a man of steel, from the White House <a href="https://x.com/WhiteHouse/status/1943493150644777199">photoshopping </a>Trump to look like Superman, to enacting tariffs on steel and approving the sale of US Steel to Japan’s Nippon Steel with a <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2025/jun/18/nippon-steel-acquires-us-steel">”golden” share</a> given to the US government.</p><p>Most recently, the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/trump-administration">Trump administration</a> announced plans to construct the largest steel plant in the US, a $15bn plant in Lee county, Iowa, to be built by India-based Mesabi Metallics.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/oct/07/trump-steel-plant-iowa-skepticism">Continue reading...</a></description>
